messages:
alex.delgado: Heads up — I'm opening a batch of 6 docs PRs to rename 'operation' -> 'execution' across the site. They include file moves, redirects, and a couple of broken anchors that need manual fixes. Need reviewers and a merge plan to avoid preview/CI collisions.

maria.k: Thanks. Can you list the PRs and which ones are high-risk?

alex.delgado: Sure — quick mapping: PR1 (concepts/ops -> execution, moves + redirects), PR2 (sdk snippets update, low risk), PR3 (api-reference anchors changed, anchor fixes + redirects), PR4 (tutorials moved, needs example updates), PR5 (nav/landing rename), PR6 (redirects-only helper). I'd call PR1, PR3, PR4 high-risk.

jake: For the anchor changes in PR3 we should include a short migration note and a redirect anchor file. Also want to avoid merging PR1 and PR4 at the same time — previews will overwrite each other and create broken permalinks in the preview environment.

alex.delgado: Agreed. Proposal: merge in this order -> PR2 (quick), PR6 (redirect helpers), then PR1 (core moves) as a canary, then PR3 (anchor fixes) after PR1 has propagated, finally PR4 and PR5. Stagger ~30–45m between the big ones. Thoughts?

sam.platform: Staggering is good. Recommend doing the big merges during the 00:00–04:00 UTC window to minimize live previews/analytics churn. Also please add label `docs-saga` and `no-automerge` to all of them. Our CI queue has been flakey; we'll bump preview workers for the window.

emma.docs: I can take PR3 review (anchors + migration note). I'll run anchor checks locally: `yarn run anchor-check || node scripts/find-broken-anchors.js` and then update the redirect YAML if needed.

alex.delgado: Thanks @emma.docs. For redirects, I'm generating them with `npm run gen-redirects` which outputs entries like:

```yaml
- from: /docs/old/path#old-anchor
  to: /docs/new/path#new-anchor
  status: 301
```

Make sure to not include fragile anchors that only exist in previews.

ci-bot: ci-bot: PR #1 preview build queued — will post link when ready.

ci-bot: ci-bot: PR #3 preview build failed: broken-anchor-check. See log: https://ci.internal/redwood/1234/logs

emma.docs: I'll dig into the failure, probably a changed heading slug. If it's a content rename we should update the heading anchor instead of adding a fragile redirect.

jake: On merge orchestration — suggest we create a tiny 'merge orchestration' thread in the PRs themselves with this checklist: 1) label `docs-saga`, 2) wait for green preview, 3) check that canonical URL responds 200 on preview, 4) merge with `squash` and include migration note.

maria.k: Who will be the final sign-off? We need at least two doc reviewers + one infra/CI ack.

emma.docs: I'll be the doc lead for signoff on content/anchors. @sam.platform will you ack CI readiness?

sam.platform: Ack — I'll monitor the preview workers and flip the extra worker toggle for the window. I'll also add a short deploy-runbook snippet to the PRs.

alex.delgado: OK assigning reviewers: emma.docs (anchors/content), jake (snippets & examples), maria.k (final pass). I'll coordinate merge timing.

docs-bot: docs-bot: Reminder — run `yarn link-checker` and `npm run gen-redirects` before marking PR ready for review.

ci-bot: ci-bot: PR #1 preview: https://preview.redwood.internal/thing/1 (status: success) :thumbsup:

alex.delgado: PR1 preview green. Waiting 40m, then merge in the low-traffic window. After merge, CI will kick for dependent PRs — hold PR3 until we see canonical pages updated.

jake: Small tip: when renaming code samples, keep an alias snippet for one release so integrations referencing examples don't break immediately. Add a short note under migration guide.

emma.docs: I fixed the broken anchor in PR3 and added the migration note. Rerunning anchor-check locally, all good.

ci-bot: ci-bot: PR3 preview: https://preview.redwood.internal/thing/3 (status: success)

alex.delgado: Great. I'll merge PR1 now, wait 35m, then merge PR3. Posting merge times in each PR before clicking the button.

maria.k: :eyes: please ping me 5m before each merge so I can watch search indexing and analytics dashboards.

alex.delgado: Will do. Thanks everyone — moving to the merge window. :shipit:
